lead: Archive seed (W38) — A week defined by long-end UST stress, fiscal-dominance confirmation from Alden, Strive/Bitcoin market-structure noise — and a robotics digest: Atlas hands for the factory, Figure’s molten decommission, and the reliability gap Physical Intelligence keeps naming.

themes.title: The bond market is the story
themes.body: 10Y yields printed multi-decade highs then eased; mortgage rates jumped to 7.28%. Alden: curve flat not steep — the argument is about the level of rates. Gromen: more UST supply as coupons reprice toward 5%+, deficits heading $2T→$3T. Mandell: “break it, buy it” between Treasury and Fed.

themes.title: Fiscal dominance as base case
themes.body: Alden’s “gradual print” framing: 7% stimulatory deficits pre-run recessions. Quality-over-quantity FinTwit posture — signal is what she objects to amid AI noise.

themes.title: Bitcoin capital markets / Strive cluster
themes.body: Walton: Buy Bitcoin; SATA at par with heavy volume. Cole: MSCI ESG hostility toward BTC cos is a $21T-benchmark problem. Mandell: BTC rally with no retracement; ASST/STRC microstructure notes.

themes.title: Energy, manufacturing, AI power
themes.body: Gromen ties dollar hegemony to manufacturing and flags Ferguson’s Law (interest > military). Pal flips the AI-power panic: China solar scale and Wright’s Law as the supply answer; Token2049 Singapore next week.

themes.title: Valuation caution (background)
themes.body: Felder’s recent posts (less frequent lately) still hammer bubble/fragility themes — useful counterweight when BTC and AI narratives run hot.

wire.title: Treasury yields pull back from multi-decade highs; bond reversal talk
wire.summary: 10Y eased after hitting highs not seen since 2002; TLT watched as oversold after a brutal quarter.

wire.title: 30-year mortgage hits 7.28%, highest since 2023
wire.summary: Biggest weekly jump in four years as long-end Treasury selloff feeds into housing costs.

wire.title: US stocks rebound modestly as yields ease from 2002 highs
wire.summary: S&P +0.2% on choppy Oct open; Micron AI memory and energy helped the bounce.

wire.title: Stablecoin issuers fill gap from China’s Treasury sales
wire.summary: SF Fed note: Tether/Circle Treasury holdings offset ~40% of China’s reductions.

sourcesNote: Weekly is a human-style distill of the daily voice set (macro + robotics). Markets: Yahoo Finance. Not investment advice.

themes.title: Hands are the product
themes.body: BD’s four-finger, 13-DOF Atlas hand is explicitly a manufacturing + sim2real design (direct drive, replaceable actuators, no pinkie). Clone’s anatomical Hand of Torso 3 is the last legacy design before a controllability-first Torso 4. Two philosophies, same bottleneck: tool use unlocks the factory.

themes.title: Ops theater → F.03
themes.body: Figure’s F.02 decommission (autonomous furnace jumps in Finland, Arnold cameo, metal artifacts) is both brand and logistics: retire proprietary hardware cleanly while the F.03 / Helix fleet takes the stage.

themes.title: Factory data flywheels
themes.body: Hyundai’s RMAC puts Atlas on a real Georgia line with a path to tens of thousands of units. UBTECH’s Liuzhou plant is already cycling humanoids off the line every ~10 minutes. Deployment volume is becoming the training set.

themes.title: Reliability over demos
themes.body: Finn: the gap between building one box and productively building boxes for hours. Jim Fan: touch still under-explored. Anthropic’s exposure math is huge; cost and unstructured environments still dominate the timeline.

wire.title: Boston Dynamics and Clone unveil new humanoid hands hours apart
wire.summary: Atlas industrial four-finger hand vs Clone anatomical hydraulics — dexterity as the week’s center of gravity.

wire.title: Atlas trains on Hyundai Georgia factory floor; 25k-unit roadmap
wire.summary: RMAC at HMGMA; parts handling first, assembly later. Data flywheel for plant AI.

wire.title: Figure decommissions F.02 fleet in Finnish arc furnace
wire.summary: Autonomous jumps into molten steel; F.03 transition story with recycled artifacts.

wire.title: Anthropic: robots + LLMs expose ~80% of US working hours
wire.summary: Exposure ≠ economics — price still the binding constraint for most physical tasks.

actionables.title: Is the bond market still the week’s primary risk?
actionables.detail: 10Y highs → ease; mortgages at 7.28%. Decide if long-end UST remains the portfolio governor for the next week, or if equity/BTC narratives reassert.

actionables.title: Mortgage 7.28% feedback into housing / credit
actionables.detail: Highest since 2023. Watch applications, builder commentary, and whether fiscal-dominance ‘gradual print’ offsets the rate hit.

actionables.title: BTC capital markets — ESG/MSCI vs SATA flows
actionables.detail: Cole’s MSCI ESG hostility framing + Walton’s SATA-at-par volume. Track whether BTC cos stay in (or leave) major benchmarks and how that hits secondary flows.

actionables.title: Factory robotics: real deployment or still theater?
actionables.detail: Hyundai RMAC (Atlas on Georgia line) + UBTECH Liuzhou cycles lean ‘real’. Figure’s F.02 melt is brand/ops. Decide which names go on the weekly watch vs remain narrative.
